changes.text: 一部明知有缺点的宪法摆在面前，签还是不签、怎么签？制宪会议最后一天：一个含糊的签署格式、几种对签名的不同理解、三个拒签的人，和议长椅背上画着的那颗太阳。

A constitution with known flaws lay on the table: sign it or not, and how? On the last day of the Constitutional Convention: an ambiguous signing formula, several readings of what a signature meant, three refusals, and a sun painted on the back of the presiding officer's chair.
1787年9月17日，制宪会议的最后一天。宪法的誊清本宣读完毕，本杰明·富兰克林站起身，手里拿着一份写好的讲稿；麦迪逊的笔记说，他是为了自己方便才把话写下来的，随后由威尔逊代为宣读。会要散了，会上仍可能有成员对桌上这份文件持有异议。摆在面前的一个问题是：签不签，怎么签。

September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and Mr. Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Some members might still have objections to the document on the table. One question before them: sign it or not, and how.
他随即动议成员签字，并提出一个现成的格式：“经出席各州一致同意，于会议中完成，9月17日……为此，我们在此签名作证。”麦迪逊记下一笔内情：这个含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者，交到富兰克林手上提出，好让它有更大的成功机会。

He then moved that members sign, and offered a convenient form: "Done in Convention by the unanimous consent of the states present, the 17th of September, &c. In witness whereof, we have hereunto subscribed our names." Madison adds a backstage note: this ambiguous form had been drawn up by Gouverneur Morris in order to gain the dissenting members, and put into Franklin's hands so that it might have the better chance of success.

这一天的争议几乎都绕着同一个动作：在文件末尾写上名字。一种解释是，莫里斯起草的那个格式把“签字”拆成了两个问题——你证明什么，你承诺什么。莫里斯把这个格式解读为只关乎“出席各州一致”这一事实，布朗特据此表示可以只作证明、不作承诺；英格索尔读作推荐；平克尼要求签名就该是承诺；伦道夫则认为两者拆不开，签了就是签了，格式再软也一样。作者推断，正因为它对不同的人意味着不同的事，多数人才能站到同一行名字底下；代价是，这行名字的含义从此需要解释。

Almost the whole day's argument circles a single act: writing a name at the foot of a page. On one reading, Morris's form split signing into two questions — what do you attest, and what do you commit to? Morris read the form as relating only to the fact that the states present were unanimous, and Blount, relieved by it, would attest that fact without committing himself; Ingersoll read the signature as a recommendation; Pinckney held that it ought to be a commitment; Randolph thought the two inseparable, a signature however softly worded being still a signature. The author's inference: precisely because the act meant different things to different men could a majority stand beneath one row of names; the price, on this inference, was that the meaning of that row would need explaining ever after.

会议日志及其他文件的去向也值得留意。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议日志或交主席保管，理由是日志若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把日志及其他文件交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

The fate of the Convention's Journals and other papers also deserves a look. In Madison's notes for the same day, King suggests that the Journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the Journals and other papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.
作者提出：可以要求在签名旁注明一句保留说明，例如“仅确认方案按程序通过，不代表认可全部条款”。这和1787年那个含糊的格式精神相通，但并非同一做法；作者也提醒，这样做会削弱“一致”的效果，需要权衡。

The author's proposal: request a short reservation beside the signature, such as attesting only that the plan passed due process and not endorsing every clause. It shares something with the ambiguous form of 1787 but is not the same device; and the author adds a caution that it weakens the effect of unanimity, which has to be weighed.
会场记录主要来自麦迪逊的笔记（1845年埃利奥特编本，维基文库）；1793年《富兰克林文集》所印讲稿可作对照，本篇未逐字比对两版。正文英文引语均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段，人物发言按笔记转述，未替任何人补写动机或心理；作者的推断均已标明为解释。

The record comes chiefly from Madison's notes (Elliot's 1845 edition, Wikisource); the speech as printed in the 1793 Works of Franklin can serve as a check, and the two have not been collated word by word here. All English quotations in the body are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes; speeches are reported as the notes give them, no motive or psychology has been supplied for anyone, and the author's inferences are marked as interpretation.

dispositions.rationale: 麦迪逊只说这个格式含糊，并说起草目的是争取异议者，没有说含糊是刻意设计的。dek 中文“有意含糊”改为“含糊”，英文“deliberately ambiguous”改为“ambiguous”。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris, in order to gain the dissenting members

dispositions.rationale: 讲话前没有证据表明已有成员公开表示异议，而且富兰克林写讲稿时并不知道会有人拒签。中英文改为“仍可能有成员持有异议”，并在本段 ev 中补上 F-E6。

evidence.quote: who may still have objections to it
he did not know that any particular member would refuse to sign his name to the instrument

dispositions.rationale: 这句归在麦迪逊名下，原文只写 ambiguous。中文删去“有意”，与英文和原文一致；英文保持原文字，同步给出。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris

dispositions.rationale: 莫里斯本人愿连同缺点接受方案，他只是指出该格式仅关乎各州一致这一事实；明确表示不承诺自己的是布朗特。中英文改为：莫里斯把格式解读为只关乎这一事实，布朗特据此可以只作证明、不作承诺。

evidence.quote: he should take it with all its faults
He remarked that the signing, in the form proposed, related only to the fact that the states present were unanimous.
would, without committing himself, attest the fact

dispositions.rationale: 英文“代价”一句原本另起，脱离了作者推断的标注。现并入推断句，并加上“on this inference”，与中文保持一致。
证据只写“Journals of the Convention”，不支持“官方”的说法，也不支持“与麦迪逊笔记是两份不同材料”的判断。中英文删去这两处，只保留去向值得留意一句。

evidence.quote: the Journals of the Convention should be either destroyed, or deposited in the custody of the president

dispositions.rationale: 中文删去没有证据支持的“有意”，改为“1787年那个含糊的格式”，与英文和原文一致；英文同步给出。
limits.0 所引书名出自1793年《富兰克林文集》，不是麦迪逊笔记。中英文把范围收窄为正文英文引语，与 limits.0 的限定一致。

evidence.quote: Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention
